risks.note: Company derives the majority of its revenue from Tata Motors Limited (CV segment) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited; it is striving to increase share of business with them while also diversifying its customer base through new products and business development, indicating high dependence on a small anchor-customer set.

Products consume mainly steel, whose prices continue to fluctuate; while customers adjust for price fluctuation, there is continuous pressure to reduce conversion and other costs, and PAN-India minimum wages were inflated significantly in the current year -- both squeeze margins absent offsetting efficiency gains.
risks.risk: Rising input costs and wage inflation

risks.note: Availability of trained manpower is a challenge amid growing demand, the new wage code, and geopolitical factors driving workmen migration between states, compounding a shortage of skilled workmen relevant to a manufacturing-labour-intensive operation.

Schedule fluctuations emerged as a potential risk during FY2026, requiring the Company to lean on established vendor partnership arrangements to scale operations up or down as needed; this points to sensitivity to OEM order-schedule volatility.

sk.overview: The DRHP frames Dhoot Transmission within India's automotive Electrical and Electronics (E&E) components industry, principally the wiring harness segment for two-wheelers (2W), three-wheelers (3W) and commercial vehicles (CV), alongside adjacent sensors/controllers, automotive switches and power supply cords. This sits within the broader Indian automotive industry (2W/3W/PV/CV/off-highway), which grew from 21.6 million units (FY20) to 28.2 million units (FY26) at a 4.6% CAGR and is projected to reach 35-45 million units by FY31 (6-8% CAGR).
